title: The Use and Usefulness of Big Data in Finance: Evidence from Financial Analysts
eligible_reason: Not a staggered adoption design. The regressor alt_data is a forecast-level indicator for whether the analyst's written report explicitly cites alternative data; it varies report by report within analyst rather than switching on permanently at an analyst-specific date. Models (Tables 3-4, 6-7) are reghdfe with firm x fiscal-year and firm x analyst (or firm x broker) fixed effects and seven time-varying forecast/analyst controls ($control_w), clustered by analyst and year-month.
design_notes: Analyst-forecast panel 2009-2019 (final_data.dta, not shipped). Table 3: reghdfe pmafe_exclude_w alt_data $control_w, absorb(gvkey_matched#year_fpe gvkey_matched#analys) vce(cluster analys ym). Table 4: commission outcome with gvkey#estimator FE (pre-2011 Ancerno sample). Table 5: calendar-time portfolio returns (SAS). Table 6: determinants of alt_data use. Table 7: category-specific indicators (app, sentiment, employee, geo, sales, satellite, search), proprietary vs widely_access splits.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: No staggered binary adoption in the reported designs.

specs.exclusion_reason: treatment indicator is not an absorbing adoption; time-varying controls; firm x year FE rather than unit + calendar-time FE
specs.controls: horizon_w firm_exp_w gen_exp_w lnnticker_w lnnfcst_w broker_size

data_files: log.log (Stata log with the paper's results run on the original data)
data_files_note: Inputs are Investext analyst reports, IBES, Compustat, CRSP, Ancerno (proprietary), Audit Analytics, EDGAR, Bloomberg; no analysis data shipped.
software_notes: Stata 17 (reghdfe) plus SAS for variable construction and Python for 8-K counts.
screener_notes: Screened from package only. The 'ft_difference_in_differences' / 'ft_two_way_fixed_effects' flags likely refer to the high-dimensional FE OLS, not to a staggered DiD.
